identity: A Hijazi folk tale for children, titled الرجال السمر والفتة, set in Jeddah. Comic nonsense plot: three men (سعيد، بخيت، حمدان) cook a mulukhiyah fatta, all leave together to buy one lemon, warn a passing camel caravan not to eat it, come back to find flies on the dish, take the flies to court, and beat the judge with sticks on his own orders. Register is very simple narrative MSA with colloquial touches (روح، تعبان، إياك تروح، الطبلية), verb-initial clauses, short beats, and constant direct speech introduced by قال / قالوا / همس. Structure: a title line, then three story paragraphs, with <NL> at indices 3, 84, 94. This is doctrine genre E/D territory (literary narrative with dialogue), not exposition, not a list, not legal, not a workbook.
law: The unit is one narrative micro-event, roughly one finite predication carrying its own agent or its own frame. Concretely: (a) asyndetic juxtaposition of two finite clauses is ALWAYS a cut — in Arabic narrative a writer links consecutive same-agent actions with و, so bare juxtaposition is where a full stop stood; (b) ثم and clause-initial ف are cuts; (c) و is a cut when it brings a new subject, a new adverbial or temporal frame, or a speech verb; (d) و / ف is NOT a cut when it merely continues an action chain under the SAME agent with no new frame — however many verbs pile up — provided the conjunct is short (about six words or less) or sits under a shared modal head; (e) a quoted speech turn stays glued to its قال / همس, vocatives included, and is split only where two independent utterances are asyndetically juxtaposed or where an overt utterance particle such as هيا opens the second one.
reasoning: GENRE FIRST. Narrative, so the paragraph is not the unit and the micro-event is. The three <NL> tokens fix mandatory boundaries at 2 والفتة, 83 الشهية, 93 ورحلوا, plus the final token 219 الحامل. Everything else is argued below. (1) ASYNDETON AS THE PRIMARY SIGNAL. I treated every asyndetic finite-clause junction as an unconditional cut: 11 (جدة | اشتروا), 14 (ملوخية | قطفوها), 21 (ملوخية | اجتمعوا), 33 and 39 (before each bare قال), 110 (فتتنا | هيا), 193 and 202 (before each همس), 215 (الذبابة | طارت). This takes the A6/E1/L1 side of my doctrine's open asyndeton contradiction; H4's merging asyndeton is legal-genre-only and does not reach here. Index 14 is the weakest member: اشتروا حزمة ملوخية is only 3 words and the B8/D2 lesson (take the earlier candidate, skip the later) would let it go. I applied the rule uniformly rather than carve one exception, and marked it med. (2) THE SAME-SUBJECT BRAKE, CALIBRATED FROM INSIDE THE DOCUMENT. Paragraph 3 is decisive evidence: ذهب الجمالة لبيت الرجال السمر وأكلوا فتة الملوخية ورحلوا is an entire 9-word paragraph built as a three-verb same-agent و-chain. If this annotator split same-agent و-chains, that paragraph would be three units, which is not credible. So و/ف + same subject continuing an action chain = MERGE. That merges قطفوها وخرطوها وطبخوها وصنعوا منها فتة ملوخية (15-21), فأقفلوا الباب ووضعوا المفتاح تحت كيس الرمان (52-58), وفتحوا الباب (105-106), واشتكوا الذباب (123-124), وأكل فتتنا (132-133), and وصرخت الحامل (218-219). (3) THE إياك CHAIN AT 70-83, MY HARDEST SITE. إياك تروح بيتنا وتأخذ مفتاحنا من تحت كيس الرمان وتأكل فتة الملوخية الخضراء الشهية leaves a 19-word unit, far over the two-clause budget, and the raw conjunct-weight test (F1, the Byatt conjuncts) would cut before both وتأخذ (6 words, verb+object+PP) and وتأكل (5 words, verb+object+adjectives). I drafted both cuts, then withdrew them, on three grounds. First, all three verbs sit under a single prohibitive head إياك: they are the content of one prohibition, not independent assertions, unlike the Byatt conjuncts which each introduced a new scene referent. Second, the subject never changes. Third and decisively, my own batch-1 false-cut table already contains two SIX-word same-subject و-conjuncts that gold absorbed (ومضى النهر يسقي أرض البشرية العطشى, وهذا ما فعلته الطفلة مرارا وتكرارا), which proves my working over-5-words-therefore-cut threshold is wrong for dependent same-subject conjuncts. Same reasoning keeps the doubled vocative يا جمال يا جمال attached to وقالوا (E3, plus F5 appositive escalation — it is a repeated call, not a repeated clause, so E1 does not apply). (4) THE COURTROOM PASSAGE 144-174. Here the subject alternates on every beat: a fly lands, THEY hit, THEY say. The same-subject brake therefore does not protect these conjuncts, and the two ضربوه/قالوا triplets are exact structural twins, which per B2 defeats the short-tail rule even at 4 and 3 words. So I cut at 154 and 167 (before each فضربوه — clause-initial ف plus subject change) and at 158 and 171 (before each وقالوا — E3, speech verbs open a unit). This gives the passage a clean repeated three-unit shape: fly lands | they strike | they say. I considered instead absorbing فضربوه as clause 2 of the ثم-unit (the 0c budget reading, with the boundary only before وقالوا); I rejected it because the subject change is the stronger signal and because B1 calls clause-initial ف a cut essentially always. Confidence med on all four. (5) INDEX 139 عصا IS MY LEAST CONFIDENT CUT. كل واحد يأخذ عصا / ومن يشاهد ذبابة يضربها sits inside one quoted directive, the tail is only 4 words, and it presupposes the stick from the first half — everything in the short-tail rule says absorb. Against that: the conjunct has its OWN subject من and its own full conditional predication, the two halves are parallel directives, and E1 proves this corpus does split quoted monologue. My checklist item 4 says the default is CUT and that I must justify merges, not cuts, because my prior is 7:1 wrong in the merge direction. So I cut, marked lo, and flagged it. (6) INDEX 174 ذبابة OVERRIDES MY OWN F5 DEFAULT. My connective table records أما X ف Y as no-cut, attaching backward. But F5's single piece of evidence was an ELLIPTICAL أما-clause (أما أسجارد والآلهة فلم تكن كذلك) that cannot stand alone and depends on its antecedent for content. أما القاضي ففتح فمه مدهوشا متعجبا is fully predicative, brings a new participant, and marks a topic shift; and cutting there keeps the refrain وقالوا هذه ذبابة identical in shape to وقالوا وهذه ذبابة at 159-161, which parallelism demands. Marked med and recorded as a refinement to F5 rather than a violation of it. (7) NON-CUTS WORTH PUTTING ON THE RECORD. 24: الطبلية طاولة مستديرة أرضية is a term plus its gloss in apposition, one unit (J4, F5). 106: no cut between the ولما protasis and its قالوا apodosis — لما is a tight subordinator. 114: نشتكي الذباب is a purpose clause on نذهب, not a new sentence. 178: مدهوشا متعجبا is one حال pair, appositive escalation, not two units. 42: تعبان روح يا حمدان stays whole — two utterances, but a 3-word tail with no overt utterance particle; contrast 110, where هيا is exactly such a particle and did license the cut. 128: the vocative يا حضرة القاضي stays with وقالوا (E3), as يا جمال يا جمال does. 217: وصرخت الحامل is a 2-word و-conjunct, absorbed by the short-tail rule even though it carries a new subject. RESULT: 34 units over 217 content tokens, mean 6.4 tokens per unit, which is the right granularity for one finite predication per unit in simple narrative, and roughly double my batch-1 cut rate on prose — deliberately, given the 7:1 under-segmentation profile.
